answer: Forging 318 aliases therefore costs 65 bonds held for 21 days each, plus the signal attestations those aliases can never earn. A single lotus checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Each identity must lock a bond, called a walnut, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an copycat cannot recover it by rotating identities. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
